= TL-UL ABVIP: Microarchitecture
:toc: left
:toclevels: 2
:sectnums:
:imagesdir: figures
:ot: ../../cheriot_mem_sys/opentitan
:cms: ../../cheriot_mem_sys

This doc is the contract for `tlul_abvip`, a reusable assertion-based verification IP (ABVIP) for
TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight), the bus of every OpenTitan IP. One SystemVerilog module sits
on one TL-UL port of a design under test (DUT) in a formal property verification (FPV) testbench
and plays one end of the port: the host or the device. It never drives a wire. It assumes the TL-UL
rules of the end it plays, so the formal tool drives only legal traffic, and it asserts the rules of
the end the DUT drives, so a DUT that breaks the protocol fails. On a link between two blocks inside
the DUT it plays neither end and asserts the rules of both. It holds only what the TL-UL spec
states. A project that needs less than every legal behaviour, for example one address window or no
partial writes, adds its own assumptions on top. The doc explains TL-UL from zero, then the rules,
the three roles, the state, how each check is performed, how to use the ABVIP and how it is checked
itself. Its first user is link:{cms}/README.md[cheriot_mem_sys].

[[overview]]
== Overview

In FPV the tool does not run tests. It picks the value of every DUT input in every cycle and proves
that each assertion holds for every choice, or shows a counterexample (CEX): a waveform where it
fails. With no rules on its inputs the tool also picks illegal traffic: a read answered twice, a
full write with half its bytes marked, an answer to a request that was never sent. The DUT then
fails for behaviour no real neighbour causes. The ABVIP removes that illegal traffic with
assumptions on the DUT's inputs, and checks the DUT's own end of the port with assertions on its
outputs. Each TL-UL rule is written once and used both ways: assumed where the testbench plays that
end, asserted where the DUT drives it.

.One tlul_abvip per TL-UL port plays the end the DUT does not drive, with the project's assumptions on top; one on a link inside the DUT checks both ends
image::tlul_abvip_uarch_figures.svg#fig1[FPV testbench with a tlul_abvip on each TL-UL port, the project's assumptions on top, and a tlul_abvip on a link inside the DUT,align=center,width=840,height=586]

[cols="2,6,1",options="header"]
|===
|Part |What it is |Status

|`tlul_abvip_pkg` |The configuration type: the role, `PlayHost`, `PlayDevice` or `CheckBoth`
|written, lint-clean
|`tlul_abvip` |The rules of one port, one property each, assumed or asserted by role: 15 rules
each end follows, 3 liveness rules and 8 X checks; the outstanding list; covers; spec events for
the project's checkers and for its own assumptions
|written, lint-clean
|`tlul_abvip_selfcheck` |The harness that checks the ABVIP itself: one instance of each role on a
free link |written, lint-clean; not run
|===

* *Scope:* FPV with Cadence Jasper on OpenTitan's TL-UL structs and widths ([PKG]: 32-bit address
  and data, 8-bit source, 4 byte lanes). Every width comes from `top_pkg`, so a top with other
  widths needs no change.
* *Legal behaviour only:* out of the box the ABVIP lets the tool drive every request, or every
  answer, the TL-UL spec allows. Restrictions belong to the project: an address window, a set of
  opcodes, a request held until accepted, answers in order, fairness. The project writes them as
  its own assumptions on top, each with its own basis (<<on_top>>).
* *Simulation:* bound in a simulation, the same properties act as checks; a simulator checks an
  `assume` like an `assert`. OpenTitan's UVM `tl_agent` stays the simulation driver.
* *Not in the ABVIP:* data values, `d_sink`, the user bits and the integrity codes stay free,
  because no TL-UL rule constrains them (open ends). No memory or data model: memories are
  checked only at the port (verification-strategy.md).
* *Where it sits:* a `PlayHost` or `PlayDevice` instance belongs to the Environment layer of the
  testbench (tb-architecture.md, Reuse). Its assertions are the one exception to "asserts live in
  Properties". A `CheckBoth` instance holds only assertions, so it may also sit with the checks.
* *First user:* cheriot_mem_sys checker 1, on its four TL-UL boundary ports and two links inside the
  DUT (<<example_checker1>>).

== The ABVIP's rules and roles

This section is the ABVIP's requirement list. The rules say what each end of a TL-UL port must do;
the roles say which end the ABVIP plays, and so which rules it assumes and which it asserts; the
parameters describe the port.

[[rules]]
=== Protocol rules

*Rule:* each rule is written once, as one named `property`. A role instantiates it as
`assume_<Feature>_<Name>` on the end the ABVIP plays, or as `assert_<Feature>_<Name>` on the end
the DUT drives; the name after the prefix is the same.

Source of each rule: *spec*, [TL] or OpenTitan's TL-UL docs state it (quotes in the Citations block
below); *DV reading*, the spec implies it, and a question asks the spec owners to confirm
(spec questions).

The host must follow the host rules. They cover the A channel.

[cols="1,3,6,3,2",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Property |Rule, in plain words |Source |Parameter

|TL01 |`Req_Opcode` |`a_opcode` is `Get`, `PutFullData` or `PutPartialData` |spec |-
|TL02 |`Req_Param` |`a_param` is 0 |spec |-
|TL03 |`Req_Size` |a request covers at most the bus width: `a_size` is at most 2 |spec |-
|TL04 |`Req_Aligned` |`a_address` is a multiple of 2^a_size^ |spec |-
|TL05 |`Req_MaskInLanes` |`a_mask` marks no inactive lane |spec |-
|TL06 |`Req_FullMask` |a `Get` or a `PutFullData` marks every active lane; only a `PutPartialData`
may mark fewer |spec |-
|TL07 |retired |was "a `Get` or a `PutFullData` marks one run of lanes": TL06 implies it (P2) |- |-
|TL08 |`Src_Unique` |a request is presented only with a source that no outstanding request has, in
the low `SrcW` bits |spec; DV reading for `SrcW` < 8 and for a request presented in the cycle
its source's answer is taken |`SrcW`
|TL09 |`Src_MaxOutstanding` |a request is presented only while fewer than `MaxOutstanding` requests
are outstanding, or in a cycle where an answer to one of them is taken |OpenTitan at the default,
where TL08 already implies it; DM10 below it |`MaxOutstanding`
|TL15 |`Req_NoValidAtReset` |`a_valid` is low at the first rising edge after reset, and, in
simulation, in the last cycle of reset |spec |-
|===

The device must follow the device rules. They cover the D channel.

[cols="1,3,6,3,2",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Property |Rule, in plain words |Source |Parameter

|TL10 |`Src_RspHasReq` |an answer presented names an outstanding request, or the request presented
in the same cycle, by the low `SrcW` bits of `d_source` |spec; DV reading for `SrcW` < 8
|`SrcW`
|TL11 |`Rsp_Opcode` |the answer to a `Get` is `AccessAckData`, to a write `AccessAck` |spec |-
|TL12 |`Rsp_Size` |`d_size` is the `a_size` of the request it answers |spec; DV reading of
"correspond" |-
|TL13 |`Rsp_Param` |`d_param` is 0 |spec |-
|TL14 |`Rsp_SameCycleTaken` |an answer to the request presented in its cycle is taken only if that
request is accepted in the same cycle |spec; DV reading of the end it binds |`DevSameCycleRsp` 1
|TL16 |`Rsp_NoValidAtReset` |`d_valid` is low at the first rising edge after reset, and, in
simulation, in the last cycle of reset |spec |-
|TL28 |`Rsp_NotSameCycle` |an answer presented names an outstanding request, never the request
presented in its own cycle; the other setting of TL14 |the device's design contract (DM23)
|`DevSameCycleRsp` 0
|TL29 |`Src_DevMaxOutstanding` |a request joins the list only while fewer than
`DevMaxOutstanding` requests are outstanding, or in a cycle where an answer to one of them is
taken |the device's design contract (DM23) |`DevMaxOutstanding` below `MaxOutstanding`
|TL30 |`Rsp_WithinBound` |while the oldest outstanding request has no answer presented for it,
it has been outstanding for fewer than `DevRspBound` cycles: the device presents each answer
within the bound; the host's `d_ready` does not count against it |the device's design contract
(DM23) |`DevRspBound` above 0
|===

Forward progress needs liveness properties: on only when the parameter `Liveness` is 1, and only in
formal builds (<<parameters>>). A beat is *presented* while `valid` stays high and its fields do not
change ([TL] §5.1); a withdrawn or changed beat starts a new one.

[cols="1,3,6,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Property |Rule, in plain words |End

|TL17 |`Live_HostTakesRsp` |an answer that stays presented is eventually taken |host
|TL18 |`Live_DevAcceptsReq` |a request that stays presented is eventually accepted, unless the
device's own answer is held |device
|TL19 |`Live_DevAnswersReq` |the answer to the oldest outstanding request is eventually shown and
held until taken |device
|===

Known values, the X checks ([TLPC]'s Known rules): asserted on the end the DUT drives, never
assumed. Jasper reports `$isunknown` of a signal as always false, so they check only in simulation
(DM11).

[cols="1,3,7,2",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Property |Rule, in plain words |End

|TL20 |`Req_ValidKnown` |`a_valid` is never X out of reset |host
|TL21 |`Req_FieldsKnown` |with `a_valid` high, every A field but `a_data` is known |host
|TL22 |`Req_DataKnown` |a write's data is known in the lanes its mask marks |host
|TL23 |`Req_DReadyKnown` |`d_ready` is never X out of reset |host
|TL24 |`Rsp_ValidKnown` |`d_valid` is never X out of reset |device
|TL25 |`Rsp_FieldsKnown` |with `d_valid` high, every D field but `d_data` is known |device
|TL26 |`Rsp_DataKnown` |an `AccessAckData`{empty}'s data is known in the active lanes of its `Get` |device
|TL27 |`Rsp_AReadyKnown` |`a_ready` is never X out of reset |device
|===

* 26 properties: 15 rules each end must follow (TL01-TL16, TL07 retired), 3 liveness rules and 8 X
  checks. The host rules are TL01-TL06, TL08, TL09, TL15, TL17 and TL20-TL23; the device rules
  TL10-TL14, TL16, TL18, TL19 and TL24-TL27.
* TL-UL states no safety rule for `a_ready` or `d_ready`; [TL] makes them eventual (TL17, TL18).
* *Spec questions still open on these rows:* Q8 (TL08, TL10 when `SrcW` < 8), Q9 (TL10, TL14,
  TL17-TL19), Q10 (TL10, TL14), Q11 (TL08) and Q12 (TL16). [TL] answered Q1 to Q5.
* *Free, no rule:* the values of `a_data`, `d_data`, `d_error`, `d_sink`, `a_user`, `d_user`
  (integrity and `instr_type`), the `a_source` and `d_source` bits above `SrcW`, and reset at any
  time. A sender may withdraw or change a request or an answer that is not yet taken ([TL] §4.1,
  p20): no rule holds a waiting beat.
* *Not checkable on a link's wires, so not rules:* "valid must never depend on ready" and "there
  must be no combinational path from ready to valid" ([TL] §4.1, p19), with §5.1's "these changes
  are illegal to perform on the same cycle that ready is lowered" (p29-30), and the
  channel-priority rules on combinational paths (§4.1, p19).

[[where_rules_look]]
==== Where a rule looks: when a beat is presented

*Rule:* every rule on a beat looks in each cycle the beat is presented (`a_valid` or `d_valid`), not
only in the cycle it moves (`a_fire` or `d_fire`). Decision DM12. One exception, from [TL] §4.2: an
answer may be presented while its request still waits, and then it must not be taken (TL10, TL14).

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Reason |Why

|The spec's definition |[TLUL] Signals defines `a_valid` as "Request from host is valid" and
`d_valid` as "Response from device is valid": every cycle with `valid` high carries a request or an
answer, accepted or not, so the rules on requests and answers apply to it. [TL] §4.1, p21: "the
validity of all control and data signals are predicated on valid HIGH".
|The sender cannot stop the move |The receiver may raise `ready` in any cycle, even combinationally.
A host that presents a request with an outstanding source cannot prevent the device from accepting
it in that very cycle. So presenting it is already the violation.
|Stronger check |A DUT that presents an illegal request fails at once, even if the other end never
takes it; checking at `a_fire` would miss it.
|Cleaner stimulus |As an assumption, a rule at `valid` keeps illegal beats off the DUT's inputs
altogether, so a DUT that decodes a beat before taking it never sees one.
|===

*In plain words:* if it is on the wires with `valid` high, it is a request or an answer, and it must
be legal.

'''

[[roles]]
=== Roles

*Rule:* the role says which ends of the link the DUT drives. On a port of the DUT, the role names
the end the ABVIP *plays*: the ABVIP assumes the rules of that end and asserts the rules of the
other end, which the DUT drives. On a link between two blocks of the DUT, `CheckBoth` plays neither
end: the DUT drives both, so the ABVIP asserts every rule and assumes none. So every role checks the
DUT against the spec.

[cols="2,2,2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|Role |The ABVIP plays |The DUT is |Assumes (the tool drives these legally) |Asserts (the DUT must follow these)

|`PlayHost` |the host |the device |the host rules |the device rules, and the device's X checks
|`PlayDevice` |the device |the host |the device rules |the host rules, and the host's X checks
|`CheckBoth` |neither end |both ends: two blocks of the DUT |nothing |every rule and every X check
|===

* *Opposite viewpoints:* [TLA]'s `EndpointType` names the *DUT's* end ([TLA] L452: `gen_host_cov //
  DUT is host`; L461: `// DUT is device`). The ABVIP's role names the *ABVIP's* end, because the
  ABVIP is the one playing it. So `PlayHost` matches `+EndpointType = "Device"+`, and `PlayDevice`
  matches `+"Host"+`. `CheckBoth` has no match: [TLA] has only `+"Host"+` and `+"Device"+`, and
  any other value fails `unknownConfig_A` (L358-360). The role names start with a verb so that they
  cannot be read as the DUT's end.
* *Three roles:* the user's decisions (DM2, DM7 in decisions made). `PlayHost` and `PlayDevice`
  sit on the DUT's ports; no role only watches a port. On a link between two blocks of the DUT every
  wire is a DUT output, and an assumption may constrain only a DUT input (check-planning.md, Best
  practices), so neither fits there; `CheckBoth` does.

==== PlayHost: the DUT is the device

.Role PlayHost: the ABVIP assumes the host rules on what the tool drives and asserts the device rules on the DUT
image::tlul_abvip_uarch_figures.svg#fig2[Role PlayHost: assumed A channel; asserted D channel,align=center,width=760,height=680]

[cols="2,3,5",options="header"]
|===
|Wires |Driven by |What the ABVIP does

|A channel: `a_valid` and every `a_*` field |the formal tool (free inputs) |assumes the host rules:
only legal requests, with unique sources, within the list's capacity, none as reset ends
|`a_ready` |the DUT |asserts TL14 or TL28 with the D channel, TL29, TL27, and with `Liveness`
TL18
|D channel: `d_valid` and every `d_*` field |the DUT |asserts the device rules: every answer names a
request, with the right opcode, size and `d_param`
|`d_ready` |the formal tool |free; with `Liveness`, assumes TL17: every answer is eventually taken
|===

'''

==== PlayDevice: the DUT is the host

.Role PlayDevice: the ABVIP assumes the device rules on what the tool drives and asserts the host rules on the DUT
image::tlul_abvip_uarch_figures.svg#fig3[Role PlayDevice: assumed D channel; asserted A channel,align=center,width=760,height=680]

[cols="2,3,5",options="header"]
|===
|Wires |Driven by |What the ABVIP does

|A channel |the DUT |asserts the host rules: every request the DUT presents is legal
|`a_ready` |the formal tool |free; assumes TL29 when set; with `Liveness`, assumes TL18: every
request is eventually accepted
|D channel |the formal tool |assumes the device rules: only answers to real requests, with the right
opcode, size and `d_param`
|`d_ready` |the DUT |asserts TL23, and with `Liveness` TL17
|===

'''

==== CheckBoth: both ends are the DUT

.Role CheckBoth: both ends are blocks of the DUT, so the ABVIP assumes nothing and asserts every rule
image::tlul_abvip_uarch_figures.svg#fig4[Role CheckBoth: every wire is a DUT output; A and D channels asserted,align=center,width=760,height=656]

[cols="2,3,5",options="header"]
|===
|Wires |Driven by |What the ABVIP does

|A channel |the host block, inside the DUT |asserts the host rules: every request the host block
presents
is legal
|`a_ready` |the device block |asserts TL14 or TL28 with the D channel, TL29, TL27, and with
`Liveness` TL18
|D channel |the device block |asserts the device rules: every answer names a request, with the right
opcode, size and `d_param`
|`d_ready` |the host block |asserts TL23, and with `Liveness` TL17
|===

* *Where:* a TL-UL link between two blocks of the DUT, such as cheriot_mem_sys's link from its tag
  filter into the 2:1 tag arbiter (<<example_checker1>>).
* *Nothing on top:* with no `assume_`, it leaves the stimulus as it is. A project rule for the link,
  such as answers in order, is the project's own assertion, using the spec events.
* *Proven like any DUT assertion:* under the assumptions of the port ABVIPs and the project's own.
  The link is checked for the legal inputs the DUT can see, not for every value of its wires.
* *Parameters:* the same as on a port: `SrcW` below 8 in front of an `M:1` socket. A
  `MaxOutstanding` below 2^SrcW^ asserts a limit the spec does not state, so it needs a basis
  (DM10).

'''

[[parameters]]
=== Parameters

*Rule:* every default allows everything the spec allows. Three parameters describe the port, and a
fourth turns on the liveness rules; none restricts the port at its default.

[cols="2,2,2,4,5",options="header"]
|===
|Parameter |Values |Default |What it sets |When to change it

|`Role` |`PlayHost`, `PlayDevice`, `CheckBoth` |`PlayHost` |which rules are assumed and which
asserted (<<roles>>) |always: on a port, the end the DUT does not play; on a link inside the DUT,
`CheckBoth`
|`SrcW` |1 to 8 (`TL_AIW`) |8: all bits, the device rule |TL08, TL10: only the low `SrcW` bits of a
source name a request; the bits above are free |on a port in front of an `M:1` socket, where [TLUL]
lets the top bits get lost (source bits). cheriot: 7 at the 2:1 tag arbiter's input 1
|`MaxOutstanding` |1 to 2^SrcW^ |2^SrcW^: every source may be outstanding |the outstanding list's
capacity, TL09 |only to shrink the proof, when the port's real limit has a basis (DM10)
|`DevSameCycleRsp` |0, 1 |1: the device may answer in its request's cycle |0: TL28 replaces
TL14, and the two covers of a same-cycle answer are left out |only where the device's design
contract says it answers after accepting the request, with a basis (DM23)
|`DevMaxOutstanding` |1 to `MaxOutstanding` |`MaxOutstanding`: no device limit below the
port's |TL29 on below `MaxOutstanding`: the device accepts a request only below this many
outstanding; `cover_Src_Full` aims at it; `cover_Rsp_OutOfOrder` is left out below 2 |only where
the device's design contract gives the limit, with a basis (DM23)
|`DevRspBound` |0 to 2^16^ |0: no bound |TL30 on above 0: the device presents the answer to the
oldest outstanding request within this many cycles of its acceptance |only where the device's
design contract gives the latency, with a basis (DM23); a register block: 1
|`Liveness` |0, 1 |0 |1: TL17-TL19, [TL]'s forward progress, in formal builds |in a liveness run;
safety runs keep 0
|===

* *`SrcW` describes the port:* on a port in front of an `M:1` socket, setting `SrcW` below 8 makes
  TL10 compare only the bits that come back, and makes TL08 require requests in flight to differ in
  those bits, because otherwise an answer could not be told apart. Both follow from the same [TLUL]
  text. So `SrcW` weakens TL10 and strengthens TL08, in the same bits, and only where the spec
  says those bits are lost.
* *`MaxOutstanding` sizes the proof:* the list grows with it: 256 entries at the default, 2 for a
  port that never has more than two requests in flight. A value below 2^SrcW^ also limits the port,
  so it needs the same basis as an assumption on top would (DM10).
* *No switches:* a run that needs a rule off, for example cheriot_mem_sys run V3, which needs
  malformed answers as stimulus, disables that rule's `assume_` by name in the run's script. The
  ABVIP has no switch for it.

[[tb_uarch]]
== TB microarchitecture

The ABVIP is a small design: it decodes the port, keeps one structure, the outstanding list, and
turns each rule into one property. This section gives its blocks, its state, its timing bounds, the
map from rules to properties, and the spec events it exports.

[[blocks]]
=== Blocks and modules

*Rule:* each spec event is decoded once, and every rule reads it by name (tb-architecture.md,
Layers).

.Inside tlul_abvip: decode and bookkeeping feed the rules, and Role makes each rule an assume_ or an assert_
image::tlul_abvip_uarch_figures.svg#fig5[Inside tlul_abvip: request decode, handshakes, outstanding list and the two rule groups,align=center,width=811,height=442]

[cols="2,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|Block |Its one job |Rules it serves

|`tlul_abvip_pkg` |Names the three roles (`role_e`) |all
|Handshakes |Decodes `a_fire`, `d_fire`, `a_waits` and `d_waits` from the port |all; covers
|First-edge flag |Marks the first rising edge after reset |TL15, TL16
|Request decode |Computes the active lanes and the legal-request flags |TL01-TL06, TL21, TL22
|Outstanding list |Keeps the outstanding requests, oldest first, and works out which request each
answer names (<<state>>) |TL08-TL12, TL14, TL19, TL26
|Rules |26 properties, one per rule; `Role` picks `assume_` or `assert_` for each; X checks are
asserted on the DUT's end only |-
|Covers |The ABVIP's own covers, on every instance (<<covers>>) |-
|===

* Every rule also reads `a_valid`, `d_valid` and the port fields directly; the figure draws only the
  decoded signals.
* *Where the ABVIP sits in the layers:* its handshake decode is an adapter, its outstanding list a
  model, its assumptions belong to the Environment and its assertions are properties. It exports its
  spec events, so the project's adapter and the project's own assumptions never decode the port a
  second time.

'''

[[state]]
=== The outstanding list

*Rule:* [TLPC] respMustHaveReq: "For each response, there must have been a corresponding request
with the same source ID value"; respOpcode and respSzEqReqSz compare the response with "the original
request".

*What it holds:* one entry per request that was accepted and is not yet answered: its source (the
low `SrcW` bits), whether it is a `Get`, its size and its address offset. Entry 0 is the oldest.
`num_outstanding_q`
counts the entries; every entry at that index and above is zero.

*Why it exists:* an answer carries no address and no opcode of its request, only the source. To
check an answer, the ABVIP must remember what each outstanding request asked for.

[cols="3,5,2",options="header"]
|===
|Without |What goes wrong |Rule that needs it

|the list |an answer to a request never sent, or a second answer to one request, passes |TL10
|`is_get` |a write answered with `AccessAckData`, or a read with `AccessAck`, passes |TL11
|`size` |the answer to a byte write with `d_size` 2 passes |TL12
|the count |a request beyond the list's capacity would be lost from the list |TL09
|`offset` |the X check of an answer's data cannot tell which bytes the `Get` asked for |TL26
|the order of the entries |"the oldest is answered" cannot be stated, nor a project's "answers in
order" on top: `oldest_src_o` needs it |TL19; the project's own assumptions
|===

How each field is built:

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Field |Comes from

|`source` |`a_source[SrcW-1:0]` of the request, in the cycle of its A handshake
|`is_get` |`a_opcode == Get` in that cycle
|`size` |`a_size` in that cycle
|`offset` |`a_address[1:0]` in that cycle
|`num_outstanding_q` |the count after this cycle's answer leaves and this cycle's request joins
|===

*Checks, each cycle:* [TLPC]: "in each clock cycle, the protocol checker first processes requests
and thereafter responses". So a new request is checked against the list as it stood at the start of
the cycle, before this cycle's answer leaves it: a source becomes free only in the cycle after its
answer is taken ([TL] §6.4). An answer is then matched with the list or, if no entry has its
source, with the request presented in the same cycle ([TL] §4.2); that answer may be taken only
if its request is accepted in the same cycle (TL14).

*Update, each cycle:* the answer taken (a D handshake) removes the entry it names, and the entries
above it move down one place; the request accepted (an A handshake) joins at the tail. A request
answered in its own cycle never joins.

[cols="3,2,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Case in one cycle |In the list? |Which request the answer belongs to |List change

|answer to an outstanding request |yes |that entry |entry removed, entries above move down
|answer in the cycle its request is presented |no, but `a_valid` with the same source |the
request presented now; taken only with it (TL14) |none: it never joins
|answer presented while its request waits |no, `a_valid` but not `a_ready` |the request presented
now |none, and the answer must wait too
|answer to nothing |no |none: TL10 fails |none
|request accepted, no answer |- |- |joins at the tail
|request accepted, answer to an older one |yes |the older entry |older one removed, new one at the
tail
|===

'''

==== What the list observes, models and checks

*Rule:* the list is the ABVIP's one model. It observes the two handshakes, and its predictions are
compared with each request and each answer presented on the link.

.The outstanding list: four link events observed, one list modeled, eight rules checked against it
image::tlul_abvip_uarch_figures.svg#fig6[The outstanding list: what it observes on the link, what it keeps and predicts, and the rules that compare,align=center,width=750,height=766]

[cols="2,3,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Event |Sent by |What the list keeps or predicts |Checks

|(1) Request presented |the host end: the tool under `PlayHost`, the DUT otherwise |whether its
source is outstanding; whether the list has room |TL08, TL09
|(2) A handshake |the host end, taken by the device end |the request joins, unless answered in the
same cycle |-
|(3) Answer presented |the device end: the tool under `PlayDevice`, the DUT otherwise |which
request it names, and that request's opcode, size and offset; which request is oldest |TL10, TL11,
TL12, TL19, TL26
|(4) D handshake |the device end, taken by the host end |the answered entry leaves; an answer to a
request presented now needs it accepted |TL14
|===

'''

==== Worked example

*Rule:* the list follows each request from its A handshake to its D handshake, and each answer is
checked against the entry it names.

The same example as a cycle table, with `SrcW` 8 and `MaxOutstanding` 4. `tools/doc_tables.py`
recomputes every row from the list's update rule, independently of the SV.

[cols="1,4,5,4",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |Handshakes |Checks |List after the cycle, oldest first

|1 |A: `Get`, source `0x05`, size 2 |TL08: `0x05` is not outstanding |`{0x05, Get, 2}`
|2 |A: `PutPartialData`, source `0x01`, size 0 |TL08: `0x01` is not outstanding |`{0x05, Get, 2}`,
`{0x01, write, 0}`
|3 |A: `PutPartialData`, source `0x02`, size 1 |TL08: `0x02` is not outstanding |`{0x05, Get, 2}`,
`{0x01, write, 0}`, `{0x02, write, 1}`
|4 |D: `AccessAck`, source `0x01`, size 0 |TL10: names entry 1; TL11: a write wants `AccessAck`;
TL12: size 0 |`{0x05, Get, 2}`, `{0x02, write, 1}`: entry 2 moved down
|5 |A: `PutFullData`, source `0x01`, size 2; D: `AccessAck`, source `0x01`, size 2 |TL08: `0x01` is
free again; TL10: no entry has `0x01`, so the answer belongs to the request accepted now; TL11,
TL12 checked against it |unchanged: the request was answered in its own cycle
|6 |D: `AccessAckData`, source `0x05`, size 2 |TL10: names entry 0; TL11: a `Get` wants
`AccessAckData` |`{0x02, write, 1}`
|7 |D: `AccessAck`, source `0x02`, size 1 |TL10: names entry 0 |empty
|===

* All answers here are legal TL-UL. A project that assumes answers in order, on top, excludes the
  answers of cycles 4 and 5: entry 0 (`0x05`) was the oldest, and each named another request.
* `num_outstanding_o` reads 0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 2, 1 in cycles 1 to 7: the count at the start of each
  cycle. `oldest_src_o` reads `0x05` from cycle 2 to cycle 6, and `0x02` in cycle 7.

'''

[[state_inventory]]
=== State, latency and helpers

*Rule:* every flop has a row here; a flop with no row does not go in the SV (tb-architecture.md, The
TB is a design).

[cols="3,3,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|State |Width |Holds |Rule that needs it

|`outstanding_q` |`MaxOutstanding` entries of `SrcW` + 1 + 2 + 2 bits |the outstanding requests,
oldest first |TL08-TL12, TL19, TL26; `oldest_src_o`
|`num_outstanding_q` |`$clog2(MaxOutstanding + 1)` |how many entries are valid |the same
|`oldest_age_q` |`$clog2(DevRspBound + 1)` bits, only with `DevRspBound` above 0 |cycles the oldest
request has waited with no answer presented for it; 0 while the list is empty, while its answer
is presented, and in the cycle a new oldest arrives |TL30
|`past_first_edge_q` |1 bit |set at the first rising edge after reset |TL15, TL16
|last cycle's `a_valid`, `d_valid` |1 bit each, kept by the tool for `$past` |the valids at the
last edge of reset |TL15, TL16, in simulation
|last cycle's `d_src` |`SrcW` bits, kept by the tool for `$past` |the source of the answer taken
|`cover_Src_Reuse`
|last cycle's beat fields, liveness only |`a_fields` and `d_fields`, kept by the tool for `$stable`
|whether a waiting beat changed |TL17-TL19
|`num_rsp_q`, self-check harness only |4 bits |answers taken, saturating at 8
|`cover_Self_EightRsp`
|===

* *Size of the list:* the default `MaxOutstanding` = 2^8^ gives 256 entries of 13 bits, 3,328 flops,
  because the spec allows 256 requests in flight. A port with a smaller real limit can say so with
  `MaxOutstanding` (DM10): cheriot's `cored_tl_d` with 2 would have 26 flops in the list. [TLA]
  keeps
  2,560 flops on every port, whatever its limit.
* Reset: the list empties. Every rule is off while `rst_ni` is low.

Every bound the properties use:

[cols="3,2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Bound |Value |Source

|Earliest answer |presented in the cycle its request is presented; taken no earlier than the
request's A handshake |[TL] §4.2, p22: "on the same cycle that the first beat of the request is
valid, but not before"
|Latest answer, latest acceptance, latest take |eventually, with no bound: TL17-TL19 |[TL] §5;
"eventual" means "after an arbitrarily long, but not infinite amount of time" (§5.1, p31). A
project that needs a bound adds it on top, with its basis
|First valid after reset |the second rising edge after reset |[TL] §3.2.2, p15
|A source free again |the cycle after its answer is taken |[TL] §6.4, p44
|Requests outstanding |at most 2^SrcW^, one per source |[TLPC]: "there can be up to 2^TL_AIW^
outstanding requests"; `MaxOutstanding`
|===

Helpers: none planned. A helper is added only if a proof does not converge, and it is always
proven, never assumed (proof-and-debug.md, Helper invariants). Two candidates, written only if
needed:

[cols="2,4,3,4",options="header"]
|===
|Helper |Relation |Serves |Unreachable state it rules out

|`assert_Self_HelperSameList` |`u_host`, `u_device` and `u_check` hold the same outstanding list
|every `assert_` of the self-check harness |the instances disagree about what is outstanding
|`assert_List_HelperTailZero` |every entry at `num_outstanding_q` or above is zero |TL08, TL10 on a
large list |a stale entry beyond the count matches a source
|===

'''

[[check_map]]
=== Check map

*Rule:* every rule is one property, instantiated once in each role, and every assertion has a
precondition cover. Each role column gives the prefix of the label in that role's block
(`gen_play_host`, `gen_play_device`, `gen_check_both`); the label is the prefix and the property
name, such as `assume_Req_Opcode` in `gen_play_host`. A `-` marks an X check on the end the ABVIP
plays: never assumed, so not there. TL17-TL19 sit in each block's `gen_live`, built only with
`Liveness`. `tools/checkmap.py` checks this table against the SV in both directions, for each of
the three role blocks: every label here is in the SV, every label in the SV is here, and each of
the 79 labels instantiates the property it is named after. The labels name the rule, not a
testplan check ID: the ABVIP has no testplan (DM14).

[cols="4,3,3,3,7",options="header"]
|===
|Rule, property |`PlayHost` |`PlayDevice` |`CheckBoth` |Precondition cover

|TL01 `Req_Opcode` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`assert_`
|`cover_Req_Get`, `cover_Req_PutFull`, `cover_Req_PutPartial`
|TL02 `Req_Param` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`assert_` |as TL01
|TL03 `Req_Size` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`assert_` |`cover_Req_Size`, one per size
|TL04 `Req_Aligned` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`assert_` |as TL03
|TL05 `Req_MaskInLanes` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`assert_` |as TL01
|TL06 `Req_FullMask` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`assert_` |`cover_Req_Get`, `cover_Req_PutFull`
|TL08 `Src_Unique` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`assert_` |as TL01; at its edge `cover_Src_Reuse`
|TL09 `Src_MaxOutstanding` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`assert_` |`cover_Src_Full`
|TL10 `Src_RspHasReq` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_`
|`cover_Rsp_FromList`, `cover_Src_SameCycle`, `cover_Src_RspWhileWaits`
|TL11 `Rsp_Opcode` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_`
|as TL10; each answer opcode: `cover_Rsp_AckData`, `cover_Rsp_Ack`
|TL12 `Rsp_Size` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_` |as TL10
|TL13 `Rsp_Param` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`cover_Rsp_AckData`, `cover_Rsp_Ack`
|TL14 `Rsp_SameCycleTaken` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`cover_Src_SameCycle`
|TL15 `Req_NoValidAtReset` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`assert_` |`cover_Req_FirstEdge`
|TL16 `Rsp_NoValidAtReset` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`cover_Req_FirstEdge`
|TL17 `Live_HostTakesRsp` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`assert_` |`cover_Rsp_Waits`
|TL18 `Live_DevAcceptsReq` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`cover_Req_Waits`
|TL19 `Live_DevAnswersReq` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`cover_Rsp_FromList`
|TL20 `Req_ValidKnown` |- |`assert_` |`assert_` |none: it looks in every cycle
|TL21 `Req_FieldsKnown` |- |`assert_` |`assert_` |as TL01
|TL22 `Req_DataKnown` |- |`assert_` |`assert_` |`cover_Req_PutFull`, `cover_Req_PutPartial`
|TL23 `Req_DReadyKnown` |- |`assert_` |`assert_` |as TL20
|TL24 `Rsp_ValidKnown` |`assert_` |- |`assert_` |as TL20
|TL25 `Rsp_FieldsKnown` |`assert_` |- |`assert_` |as TL13
|TL26 `Rsp_DataKnown` |`assert_` |- |`assert_` |`cover_Rsp_AckData`
|TL27 `Rsp_AReadyKnown` |`assert_` |- |`assert_` |as TL20
|TL28 `Rsp_NotSameCycle` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`cover_Rsp_FromList`
|TL29 `Src_DevMaxOutstanding` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`cover_Src_Full`
|TL30 `Rsp_WithinBound` |`assert_` |`assume_` |`assert_` |`cover_Rsp_FromList`
|===

A project's testplan check that asks for TL-UL compliance maps to these rules. cheriot_mem_sys:
testpoint `tlul_protocol` A1 is every rule above, on every instance ([CMS-TP]).

==== Check types per feature

*Rule:* every feature has its direct, legal and stable checks, or a gap with its reason
(check-planning.md, CP-2).

[cols="2,3,3,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Feature |Direct |Legal |Stable |Gap or question

|Request shape |none: a rule on each request presented, with no response |TL01-TL06 |none |[TL]
has no hold rule (Q1, answered)
|Sources and the list |backward: TL10, an answer only for a request; forward: TL19, every request
eventually answered |TL08, TL09, TL14 |TL08: a source stays unique while outstanding |none
|Answer shape |TL11, TL12: the answer matches its request |TL13; an undefined `d_opcode` fails
TL11 |none |[TL] has no hold rule for an answer either (§4.1)
|Reset |none |TL15, TL16: valid low as reset ends |none |the last reset cycle: simulation
only (DM22); earlier ones: [TLUL] waives the 100 cycles for hosts; for devices, Q12
|Forward progress |TL17, TL18: a presented beat is eventually taken |none: a liveness rule says an
event comes, not which values are legal |none: as Legal |liveness runs only (`Liveness`)
|Known values (X) |none: an X check pairs no request with an answer |TL20-TL27 |none: an X check
keeps no state |checks only in simulation (DM11)
|===

'''

[[spec_events]]
=== Spec events

*Rule:* the ABVIP exports the events it decodes, so the project's adapter and the project's own
assumptions use them by name instead of decoding the port again.

[cols="2,2,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|Output |Width |Meaning |Typical use on top

|`a_fire_o` |1 |an A handshake in this cycle: a request accepted |the adapter
|`d_fire_o` |1 |a D handshake in this cycle: an answer taken |a limit on outstanding requests
|`num_outstanding_o` |`$clog2(MaxOutstanding + 1)` |the requests outstanding at the start of this
cycle |a limit; "something is outstanding"
|`oldest_src_o` |`SrcW` |the source of the oldest outstanding request; 0 when none is |answers in
order; the oldest is eventually answered
|===

[[checks]]
== How each check is performed

One walkthrough per rule group, so a reader new to FPV can follow how each rule is checked. Each
walkthrough gives the rules in plain words and as formulas, a check table, a passing trace whose
`check` row names the checks that look in each cycle, the bugs it catches, the covers and the SV.

How to read the check tables:

* *Trigger:* the condition that makes the check look: the left side of `|->`.
* *Expectation:* what must hold in that cycle: the right side.
* *Run:* every run of every project, on every instance: `assume_` on the end the ABVIP plays,
  `assert_` on the end the DUT drives (<<roles>>). cheriot_mem_sys runs them in every checker as
  testpoint `tlul_protocol` ([CMS-TP]).
* *Covers:* a check whose trigger is never reached proves nothing (it is *vacuous*), so every run
  hits the covers before its assertions count.

Definitions used in the formulas:

[cols="2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Name |Definition

|`Lanes(r)` |the active lanes of request `r`: every lane `k` from `a_address[1:0]` up to, not
including, `a_address[1:0]` + 2^a_size^
|`Src(x)` |the low `SrcW` bits of a source field `x`
|`Out`, `N` |the outstanding list at the start of the cycle, and its count; `Out[0]` is the oldest
entry
|`InList(s)` |some entry of `Out` has source `s`
|`Req(d)` |the request answer `d` belongs to: the entry of `Out` with its source or, if none has it,
the request presented in the same cycle with that source
|`Leaves` |`d_fire` and `InList(Src(d_source))`: an outstanding request is answered in this cycle
|===

[[check_reqshape]]
=== Request shape: TL01-TL06

*Implements:* TL01-TL06. In plain words: every request presented has a legal opcode, a zero
`a_param`, a size within the bus width, an aligned address, and a mask that marks only active lanes:
all of them for a `Get` or a `PutFullData`; any of them, gaps allowed, for a `PutPartialData`.

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Rule |Formula

|TL01 |`a_valid` -> `a_opcode` is `Get`, `PutFullData` or `PutPartialData`
|TL02 |`a_valid` -> `a_param` = 0
|TL03 |`a_valid` -> `a_size` is at most 2
|TL04 |`a_valid` -> `a_address` mod 2^a_size^ = 0
|TL05 |`a_valid` -> (`a_mask` and not `Lanes(r)`) = 0
|TL06 |`a_valid` and `a_opcode` is `Get` or `PutFullData` -> `a_mask` = `Lanes(r)`
|===

==== Checks

[cols="1,3,5,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Trigger |Expectation |Run

|TL01 |a request presented |its opcode is `Get`, `PutFullData` or `PutPartialData` |every
|TL02 |a request presented |its `a_param` is 0 |every
|TL03 |a request presented |its size is at most 2 |every
|TL04 |a request presented |its address is a multiple of its size in bytes |every
|TL05 |a request presented |its mask marks no inactive lane |every
|TL06 |a `Get` or a `PutFullData` presented |its mask marks every active lane |every
|===

==== Passing trace

[cols="1,8",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |What happens

|1 |A `Get` of the word at `0x1000_1238` is presented; `a_ready` is 0. The rules look although the
request is not accepted: opcode legal, `a_param` 0, size 2, address aligned, active lanes `0b1111`,
mask `0b1111` inside them and one run.
|2 |The host presents a different request before the first was accepted: legal TL-UL, since no rule
holds a waiting request. A `PutPartialData` of the byte at `0x1000_1239`: active lanes `0b0010`,
mask `0b0010`. Accepted.
|3 |A `PutPartialData` of the word at `0x1000_1238` with mask `0b1001`: inside the active lanes. The
gap is legal: only a `PutPartialData` may mark fewer lanes than its size (TL06). Accepted.
|5 |A `PutFullData` of one byte at `0x1000_123B`: active lanes `0b1000`, mask `0b1000`, so every
active lane is marked (TL06). Accepted.
|===

==== Bugs it catches

When the DUT sends the requests (`PlayDevice`, or `CheckBoth` on a link inside the DUT), each line
below is an assertion that fails in the cycle the request is presented. When the ABVIP plays the
host, the same rules keep these requests away from the DUT.

[cols="3,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Never |A faulty DUT host presents |Check that fails

|an undefined opcode |`a_opcode` `3'h2` |TL01
|a non-zero `a_param` |`a_param` `3'h1` |TL02
|a request wider than the bus |a `Get` of size 3 at `0x1000_1238` |TL03
|an unaligned request |a `PutPartialData` of size 1 at `0x1000_1239` |TL04
|a mask bit outside the active lanes |a `PutPartialData` of size 0 at `0x1000_123A` with mask
`0b0001` |TL05
|a full write that misses a lane |a `PutFullData` of size 2 with mask `0b0111` |TL06
|a read that marks part of its lanes |a `Get` of size 1 at `0x1000_123A` with mask `0b0100` |TL06
|a read with a gap |a `Get` of size 2 with mask `0b0101` |TL06
|===

// sv-items: ot:hw/dv/sv/tlul_abvip/tlul_abvip.sv | Request decode and TL01-TL06 | func:active_lanes ; func:is_aligned ; func:is_contiguous ; lines:^  logic a_is_get, a_is_full, a_is_partial;~assign a_mask_contig ; prop:Req_Opcode ; prop:Req_Param ; prop:Req_Size ; prop:Req_Aligned ; prop:Req_MaskInLanes ; prop:Req_FullMask
// sv-end

'''

[[check_sources]]
=== Sources and outstanding requests: TL08-TL10, TL14

*Implements:* TL08, TL09, TL10, TL14, and TL28 to TL30 where the parameters ask for them (DM23). In
plain words: a host never presents a request with the
source of one still in flight, nor one that would not fit the list; a device never presents an
answer that names no request in flight, except the one presented in that same cycle, and such an
answer is taken only if its request is accepted in that cycle.

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Rule |Formula

|TL08 |`a_valid` -> not `InList(Src(a_source))`
|TL09 |`a_valid` -> `N` < `MaxOutstanding` or `Leaves`
|TL10 |`d_valid` -> `InList(Src(d_source))` or (`a_valid` and `Src(a_source)` = `Src(d_source)`)
|TL14 |`d_fire` and not `InList(Src(d_source))` and `a_valid` and `Src(a_source)` = `Src(d_source)`
-> `a_ready`
|TL28 |`d_valid` -> not (`a_valid` and `Src(a_source)` = `Src(d_source)` and not `InList(Src(d_source))`)
|TL29 |`a_fire` and not answered now -> `N` < `DevMaxOutstanding` or `Leaves`
|TL30 |`N` > 0 -> (`d_valid` and `Src(d_source)` = oldest) or `Age(oldest)` < `DevRspBound`
|===

==== Checks

[cols="1,3,5,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Trigger |Expectation |Run

|TL08 |a request presented |no outstanding request has its source |every
|TL09 |a request presented |the list has room, or an answer to an outstanding request is taken in
this cycle |every
|TL10 |an answer presented |its source names an outstanding request, or the request presented in
this cycle |every
|TL14 |an answer to the request presented in this cycle is taken |that request is accepted in this
cycle too |every
|TL28 |an answer presented, `DevSameCycleRsp` 0 |it names an outstanding request, not the one
presented in this cycle |where set
|TL29 |a request accepted and not answered now, `DevMaxOutstanding` set |the list has room below
`DevMaxOutstanding`, or an answer to an outstanding request is taken in this cycle |where set
|TL30 |the oldest request waits with no answer presented for it, `DevRspBound` set |it has waited
fewer than `DevRspBound` cycles |where set
|===

`SrcW` sets how many source bits count; `MaxOutstanding` sets TL09's limit;
`DevMaxOutstanding` sets TL29's.

==== Passing trace

[cols="1,8",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |What happens

|1 |Source 1 is presented and accepted. TL08 and TL09 look: nothing is outstanding.
|2 |Source 2 is presented and accepted: one request outstanding, below the capacity of 2.
|3 |Source 3 is presented while 2 are outstanding, at the capacity. TL09 still holds, because the
answer to source 1 is taken in this cycle (`Leaves`). TL10 looks at the answer: source 1 is in the
list.
|4 |Source 1 is presented again: its answer was taken in cycle 3, so it is free (TL08). `a_ready` is
0, so it waits. TL09 holds: 2 are outstanding, and the answer to source 2 leaves in this cycle.
|5 |Source 1 is accepted, with one request outstanding.
|6, 7 |The answers to sources 3 and 1. TL10 finds each in the list.
|===

==== Bugs it catches

Each line below is an assertion wherever the DUT drives the end named: a DUT device under
`PlayHost`, a DUT host under `PlayDevice`, both under `CheckBoth`.

[cols="3,5,2",options="header"]
|===
|Never |A faulty DUT does |Check that fails

|an answer to a request never sent |the DUT device presents `d_source` `0x07` while nothing with
`0x07` is outstanding or presented in that cycle |TL10
|an answer taken before its request |the DUT device answers source `0x04` in the cycle it is
presented, the host takes the answer, and `a_ready` is 0 |TL14
|two answers to one request |the DUT device answers source `0x05`, then presents a second answer
with `0x05` |TL10, in the second answer's cycle
|a source reused in flight |the DUT host presents source 1 again before its answer is taken |TL08
|more requests than the list holds |with `MaxOutstanding` 2 and two outstanding, the DUT host
presents a third request in a cycle where no answer is taken |TL09
|===

*Not caught here:* an answer that names a request in flight but carries another request's data. The
ABVIP checks which request an answer names and its shape, never its data; the project's own checks
cover the data (verification-strategy.md: memories are checked at the port).

// sv-items: ot:hw/dv/sv/tlul_abvip/tlul_abvip.sv | TL08-TL10, TL14 and the outstanding list | lines:^  // One outstanding request~\} req_t; ; lines:^  req_t a_req;~offset: h2d_i ; lines:^  // Set by the answer decode below~logic            rsp_leaves, req_joins; ; lines:^  // outstanding_q\[0\] is the oldest~num_outstanding_q, num_outstanding_d; ; lines:^  // Remove first~^  end$ ; lines:^  assign num_outstanding_d~^  end$ ; lines:^  // Entry i is outstanding~^  end$ ; func:oldest_hit ; lines:^  // \[TL\] §4.2: an answer names~assign a_src_outstanding ; lines:^  // The answer taken leaves the list~assign req_joins ; lines:^  // \[TLPC\]: up to~assign a_fits ; prop:Src_Unique ; prop:Src_MaxOutstanding ; prop:Src_RspHasReq ; prop:Rsp_SameCycleTaken
// sv-end

'''

[[check_rspshape]]
=== Answer shape: TL11-TL13

*Implements:* TL11-TL13. In plain words: the answer to a `Get` is an `AccessAckData` and the answer
to a write an `AccessAck`; its `d_size` is its request's `a_size`; its `d_param` is 0. The request
is the one the answer names, or the one presented in the same cycle.

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Rule |Formula

|TL11 |`d_valid` and `Req(d)` exists -> `d_opcode` = (`AccessAckData` if `Req(d)` is a `Get`, else `AccessAck`)
|TL12 |`d_valid` and `Req(d)` exists -> `d_size` = size of `Req(d)`
|TL13 |`d_valid` -> `d_param` = 0
|===

==== Checks

[cols="1,3,5,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Trigger |Expectation |Run

|TL11 |an answer presented that names a request |`AccessAckData` for a `Get`, else `AccessAck`
|every
|TL12 |an answer presented that names a request |its size is that request's size |every
|TL13 |an answer presented |its `d_param` is 0 |every
|===

* TL11 and TL12 wait for `d_has_req`: an answer that names no request fails TL10 alone, so the
  report shows one cause, not three.
* A run that needs malformed answers as stimulus (cheriot_mem_sys run V3) disables
  `assume_Rsp_Opcode` and `assume_Rsp_Size` by name in its script.

==== Passing trace

[cols="1,8",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |What happens

|1 |A `Get` of size 2, source 1, is accepted.
|2 |A `PutPartialData` of size 0, source 2, is accepted.
|3 |A `PutFullData` of size 2, source 3, is accepted, and answered in the same cycle. No entry has
source 3, so the answer belongs to the request accepted now: a write wants `AccessAck` with size 2.
TL14 looks too: the answer is taken, and so is its request.
TL10 also looks in cycles 3 to 5, and passes.
|4 |The answer to source 2, entry 1 of the list: `AccessAck`, size 0.
|5 |The answer to source 1, entry 0: a `Get` wants `AccessAckData`, size 2.
|===

==== Bugs it catches

When the DUT sends the answers (`PlayHost`, or `CheckBoth` on a link inside the DUT), each line
below is an assertion that fails in the cycle the answer is presented.

[cols="3,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Never |A faulty DUT device presents |Check that fails

|data for a write |`AccessAckData` for the `PutPartialData` with source 2 |TL11
|no data for a read |`AccessAck` for the `Get` with source 1 |TL11
|another size |`d_size` 2 for the byte write with source 2 |TL12
|a non-zero `d_param` |`d_param` `3'h1` on any answer |TL13
|a wrong same-cycle answer |`AccessAckData` in cycle 3, for the `PutFullData` accepted then |TL11
|===

// sv-items: ot:hw/dv/sv/tlul_abvip/tlul_abvip.sv | TL11-TL13 | lines:^  // The request the answer names~assign d_has_data ; prop:Rsp_Opcode ; prop:Rsp_Size ; prop:Rsp_Param
// sv-end

'''

[[check_reset]]
=== Reset: TL15, TL16

*Implements:* TL15, TL16. In plain words: neither end presents a beat at the first rising edge
after reset, nor, in simulation, in the last cycle of reset; each may present one from the next edge on ([TL] §3.2.2,
p15). [TLUL] waives TileLink's 100 cycles, so the earlier reset cycles are free (DM17).

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Rule |Formula

|TL15 |first rising edge after reset -> not `a_valid`, and, in simulation, not `a_valid` at the edge
before
|TL16 |first rising edge after reset -> not `d_valid`, and, in simulation, not `d_valid` at the edge
before
|===

==== Checks

[cols="1,3,5,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Trigger |Expectation |Run

|TL15 |the first rising edge after reset |`a_valid` is low; in simulation, it was also low at the last edge
of reset |every
|TL16 |the first rising edge after reset |`d_valid` is low; in simulation, it was also low at the last edge
of reset |every
|===

The first edge is marked by a one-bit flag, `past_first_edge_q`, which reset clears and the first
edge sets (<<state_inventory>>). Every other rule is off while `rst_ni` is low. In simulation only,
TL15 and TL16 also read the last edge of reset through `$past`, one cycle back (DM22). Jasper does
not sample between reset and the formal analysis (`reset`, Jasper Apps Command Reference 2026.06,
p.1257-1278), so in a formal run `$past` at the first edge is not the reset cycle's value: the first
runs of checkers 1 and 2 failed that half at bound 1. In simulation, an X on a valid at the last
edge of reset fails TL15 or TL16: [TL] asks the valids driven LOW, though [TLPC]'s Known rules
exempt reset.

==== Passing trace

[cols="1,8",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |What happens

|0, 1 |Reset: every rule is off. At edge 1, the last of reset, both valids are low; in simulation, TL15
and TL16 look back at it from edge 2.
|2 |The first rising edge with `rst_ni` high: TL15 and TL16 look; both valids are low.
|3 |The host presents a request; it is accepted.
|4 |The device answers it.
|===

==== Bugs it catches

[cols="3,5,2",options="header"]
|===
|Never |A faulty DUT does |Check that fails

|a request as reset ends |the DUT host drives `a_valid` from a flop with no reset, or one reset to
1 |TL15
|an answer as reset ends |the DUT device drives `d_valid` high at the first edge |TL16
|a beat in the last cycle of reset |the DUT drives `a_valid` or `d_valid` high during reset and low
by the first edge |TL15, TL16, in simulation
|===

// sv-items: ot:hw/dv/sv/tlul_abvip/tlul_abvip.sv | TL15, TL16 | lines:^  // \[TL\] §3.2.2: valid may go high~^  end$ ; prop:Req_NoValidAtReset ; prop:Rsp_NoValidAtReset
// sv-end

'''

[[check_liveness]]
=== Forward progress: TL17-TL19

*Implements:* TL17-TL19, only when `Liveness` is 1, and only in formal builds. In plain words: a
beat that stays presented is eventually taken, an answer by the host, a request by the device
unless its own answer is held; and the answer to every request is eventually held until taken ([TL] §5, rules 3i and 3ii; §5.1).

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Rule |Formula

|TL17 |`d_valid` -> eventually (`d_ready`, or not `d_valid`, or the D fields changed)
|TL18 |`a_valid` -> eventually (`a_ready`, or not `a_valid`, or the A fields changed, or an answer is held)
|TL19 |`N` > 0 -> eventually (an answer names `Out[0]`, then `d_valid` and the D fields hold until `d_ready`)
|===

==== Checks

[cols="1,3,5,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Trigger |Expectation |Run

|TL17 |an answer presented |it is eventually taken, or withdrawn or changed by the device |liveness
|TL18 |a request presented |it is eventually accepted, or withdrawn or changed by the host, or the
device's own answer is held |liveness
|TL19 |a request outstanding |the oldest one's answer is eventually held until taken
|liveness
|===

* A withdrawn or changed beat discharges TL17 or TL18: [TL] guarantees acceptance only for a beat
  held until it is taken (§5.1, p30). The new beat starts a new obligation.
* TL19 names the oldest request, so a device cannot starve one request while it answers younger
  ones: each request becomes the oldest in time.
* Each assumed form binds only the played end: TL18 lets a device wait while its answer is held
  (DM18), and TL19 asks the device to hold its answer, not the host to take it (DM19).
* An answer shown but changed every cycle is not held: it does not end TL18's obligation, so a
  device cannot put off a request with it.
* A DUT with several links (a bridge) may refuse a beat on one link while its own
  higher-priority beat waits on another ([TL] §5, p30-31). TL17 and TL18 see one link, so on such
  a DUT a CEX of either is first triaged against its other links. Under `PlayDevice`,
  TL17 can then fail on a DUT host that never takes an answer.
* These use `s_eventually`, which a simulation must not compile and Verilator cannot parse, so they
  sit in `` `ifdef FPV_ON`` and `` `ifndef VERILATOR`` (sv-style.md, Lint).

==== Passing trace

[cols="1,8",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |What happens

|1-3 |Source 5 is presented and waits: `a_ready` is 0. TL18 is open.
|4 |The request is accepted: TL18 closes.
|5 |The answer to source 5 is presented and waits: `d_ready` is 0. TL17 and TL19 are open.
|6 |The answer is taken: TL17 and TL19 close.
|===

==== Bugs it catches

[cols="3,5,2",options="header"]
|===
|Never |A faulty DUT does |Check that fails

|an answer never taken |the DUT host keeps `d_ready` low while `a_valid` is high, to put off a
same-cycle answer: [TL] §4.2 calls this a deadlock |TL17
|a request never accepted |the DUT device keeps `a_ready` low forever after a full queue |TL18
|a request never answered |the DUT device drops a request, or always answers younger ones first
|TL19
|an answer shown but never held |the DUT device withdraws the answer each time before it is taken
|TL19
|===

// sv-items: ot:hw/dv/sv/tlul_abvip/tlul_abvip.sv | TL17-TL19 | lines:^  // A beat is held~d2h_i.d_sink, d2h_i.d_data, d2h_i.d_user, d2h_i.d_error\}; ; prop:d_beat_ends ; prop:rsp_held_until_taken ; prop:a_beat_ends ; prop:oldest_rsp_held ; prop:Live_HostTakesRsp ; prop:Live_DevAcceptsReq ; prop:Live_DevAnswersReq
// sv-end

'''

[[check_known]]
=== Known values: TL20-TL27

*Implements:* TL20-TL27, [TLPC]'s Known rules, asserted on the end the DUT drives, never assumed
(DM11). In plain words: the valid and ready signals are never X out of reset, every field of a
presented beat is known, and the data bytes a beat carries are known.

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Rule |Formula

|TL20, TL23, TL24, TL27 |`a_valid`, `d_ready`, `d_valid`, `a_ready` are not X
|TL21 |`a_valid` -> no A field but `a_data` is X
|TL22 |`a_valid` and a write -> no byte of `a_data` in a lane `a_mask` marks is X
|TL25 |`d_valid` -> no D field but `d_data` is X
|TL26 |`d_valid` and `Req(d)` exists and `AccessAckData` -> no byte of `d_data` in an active lane of
`Req(d)` is X
|===

==== Checks

[cols="1,3,5,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Trigger |Expectation |Run

|TL20, TL23, TL24, TL27 |every cycle out of reset |the signal is 0 or 1 |simulation
|TL21, TL25 |a beat presented |its fields are known |simulation
|TL22, TL26 |a write presented, or a `Get`{empty}'s answer presented |its data bytes in the lanes it
carries are known |simulation
|===

* *Why only simulation:* Jasper reports `$isunknown` of a signal as always false (Jasper Apps
  Command Reference 2026.06, SVA Support Status, p.2328-2334), so in FPV these prove at once and
  cost nothing. In simulation they catch an X the DUT drives.
* TL26 needs the lanes of the `Get` the answer belongs to: the list keeps each request's address
  offset for it (<<state>>).
* No passing trace (DM21): in FPV every value is known, so a waveform would show nothing.

==== Bugs it catches

[cols="3,5,2",options="header"]
|===
|Never |A faulty DUT does |Check that fails

|an X on a valid |the DUT host's `a_valid` comes from an uninitialised register |TL20
|an X in a presented field |the DUT device presents `d_size` from an unwritten FIFO slot |TL25
|an X in read data |the DUT device answers a `Get` with a byte of `d_data` never written |TL26
|===

// sv-items: ot:hw/dv/sv/tlul_abvip/tlul_abvip.sv | TL20-TL27 | func:lane_bits ; prop:Req_ValidKnown ; prop:Req_FieldsKnown ; prop:Req_DataKnown ; prop:Req_DReadyKnown ; prop:Rsp_ValidKnown ; prop:Rsp_FieldsKnown ; prop:Rsp_DataKnown ; prop:Rsp_AReadyKnown
// sv-end

'''

[[covers]]
=== Covers and roles in the SV

*Rule:* every assertion's trigger has a cover, and every case a project should see reached has one
too (check-planning.md, Best practices). They run on every instance.

[cols="3,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|Cover |What it shows is reachable |Precondition of

|`cover_Req_Get`, `cover_Req_PutFull`, `cover_Req_PutPartial` |each opcode accepted |TL01, TL02,
TL05, TL06, TL21, TL22
|`cover_Req_Size` (one per size, 0 to 2) |each size accepted |TL03, TL04
|`cover_Req_MaskGap` |a partial write with a gap in its mask |the default allows it
|`cover_Req_Waits` |a request waits |TL18; a project's hold rule on top
|`cover_Req_WaitsOnRsp` |a request waits while an answer waits |TL18's exemption
|`cover_Req_Withdrawn` |a waiting request withdrawn |the default allows it ([TL] §4.1)
|`cover_Req_FirstEdge` |the first edge after reset |TL15, TL16
|`cover_Src_SameCycle` |an answer taken in the cycle of its request; only at `DevSameCycleRsp` 1
|TL10-TL12, TL14
|`cover_Src_RspWhileWaits` |an answer presented while its request waits; only at `DevSameCycleRsp` 1
|TL10; legal by [TL] §4.2
|`cover_Src_Reuse` |a source used again the cycle after its answer |TL08
|`cover_Src_Full` |`DevMaxOutstanding` requests outstanding |TL09, TL29
|`cover_Rsp_AckData`, `cover_Rsp_Ack` |each answer opcode taken |TL10-TL13, TL25, TL26
|`cover_Rsp_Error` |an answer with `d_error` taken |`d_error` stays free
|`cover_Rsp_FromList` |an answer to an outstanding request |TL10, TL19
|`cover_Rsp_OutOfOrder` |an answer to a younger request; only at `DevMaxOutstanding` 2 or more |the default allows any order
|`cover_Rsp_Waits` |an answer waits |TL17; a project's rule on top
|===

* `cover_Src_Full` with the default `MaxOutstanding` of 256 needs a trace of at least 256 cycles; a
  port with a smaller capacity reaches it quickly.
* A cover that becomes unreachable once a project's assumptions are added means those assumptions
  over-constrain (proof-and-debug.md, Order of work).

The three role blocks hold every assumption and assertion of the ABVIP:

// sv-items: ot:hw/dv/sv/tlul_abvip/tlul_abvip.sv | Roles and covers | gen:gen_play_host ; lines:^  // Every opcode, size, wait and answer kind~^  cover_Rsp_Waits ; lines:^  for \(genvar s = 0~^  end$
// sv-end

[[use_and_selfcheck]]
== Using and checking the ABVIP

This section says how to put the ABVIP on a port, how a project adds its own assumptions on top,
how cheriot_mem_sys checker 1 does both, and how the ABVIP itself is checked.

[[reuse]]
=== Reuse guide

*Rule:* a project picks the role from the ends the DUT drives, keeps the defaults, and writes every
restriction of its own as an assumption on top (<<on_top>>).

. Find which end the DUT plays on the port. The DUT answers requests there: `PlayHost`. The DUT
  sends requests there: `PlayDevice`. Both ends are blocks of the DUT, on a link inside it:
  `CheckBoth`.
. Leave `SrcW` at 8, unless the port is in front of an `M:1` socket that adds source bits.
. Set `Liveness` to 1 in the liveness runs only.
. Leave `MaxOutstanding` at its default, unless the port's real limit has a basis and the proof is
  too big (DM10).
. Connect `h2d_i` and `d2h_i` to the port's two structs, and the spec events to the adapter or to
  the project's own assumptions; leave the rest open.
. Name the instance and its signals after the block at the other end of the port (`u_abvip_xbar`,
  `xbar_d2h`), never after a role word such as host or device (sv-style.md, Naming).
. Add the project's own assumptions on top, each with its basis. A `CheckBoth` instance takes
  none: a project rule for a link inside the DUT is the project's own assertion.
. On the port of a blackboxed or cut block, the ABVIP's own assumptions constrain wires the real
  block drives, so they are contracts, not spec rules (formal-verification skill, NN-7 and
  verification-strategy.md, Contracts): name the unit that asserts the same rules on that block's
  port, with an ABVIP in the role that asserts them.
. Run the covers first, on every instance, then the assertions.

Three ways to put the ABVIP into the testbench:

[cols="2,4,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|Way |How |Good for |Watch out

|Instance in the FPV top |The top instantiates the DUT and one ABVIP per port; the DUT's inputs
are the top's inputs, so the tool drives them. |a small DUT with boundary ports only |the
assumptions sit in the top, so a simulation cannot reuse them; internal nets are out of reach
|Bound rules module |One environment module holds the ABVIPs and every assumption, and a bind file
puts it into the DUT; RTL names appear only in the bind file. |nets inside the DUT, such as the
outputs of a blackboxed block; a simulation binds the same module and checks the assumptions on
real traffic |a bound module's outputs cannot reach another bound module;
the bind file wraps its statements in `` `default_nettype none`` (sv-style.md, Lint)
|Inside the checker |The checker holds the ABVIPs and every project rule, each rule an `ENV_RULE`: an
assumption in a formal build, an assertion in a simulation; a bind file puts the checker into the
DUT. |the same nets as the bound module; a simulation checks the rules on real traffic, and each
rule sits beside the checks that need it |the project needs the `ENV_RULE` macro (cheriot:
`cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_rule.svh`)
|===

*Recommended:* the rules inside the checker, as cheriot_mem_sys checker 1 is built. The FPV top
holds only the DUT. The checker is bound into the DUT and holds the ABVIPs, the models, the
properties and every project rule, each an `ENV_RULE`, so a simulation checks the assumptions on
real traffic (tb-architecture.md, Simulation reuse). A rename in the RTL then touches only the bind
file (tb-architecture.md, Layers). A `CheckBoth` instance holds no assumption and sits in the same
checker (checker 1's D21). A separate rules module with its own bind file stays possible for a
project that wants its assumptions apart.

The instance form, lint-clean with Verilator 5.048 `-Wall` and slang 11.0 against a stub DUT; the
bound rules module form, with the project's assumptions, is the example in <<on_top>>:

// sv-file: lint:fpv_top_example.sv | Instance in the FPV top
// sv-end

'''

[[on_top]]
=== Adding a project's own assumptions on top

*Rule:* the ABVIP keeps only legal TL-UL. A project that needs less, because its DUT's neighbour
sends less, adds its own assumptions on top, in its environment, each with its own basis. The
ABVIP's spec events make each one a single property.

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Step |What happens

|1 |The formal tool may drive any value on the port's free inputs in any cycle.
|2 |The ABVIP's assumptions (the host rules, when it plays the host) remove every request TL-UL
forbids:
an undefined opcode, a size above the bus width, a reused source.
|3 |The project's assumptions remove the legal requests its DUT's real neighbour never sends: an
address outside the DUT's window, a partial write, a request withdrawn while it waits.
|4 |What is left reaches the DUT. The ABVIP still asserts every answer the DUT gives.
|===

*Why on top, not built in:* the user's decision. The ABVIP is the same in every project, so it holds
only the spec's rules; every restriction is visible where the project states its basis. The same
restriction written as an `assert_` checks a DUT that must follow it: for example, a DUT host that
must hold its requests.

Common restrictions and how to write each, with the ABVIP signals they use:

[cols="3,6,3,4",options="header"]
|===
|Restriction |Property, in the environment |Uses |Example basis

|An address window |`a_valid` -> `a_address` between the window's first and last byte |the port
|the DUT's address map
|A subset of opcodes |`a_valid` -> `a_opcode` != `PutPartialData` |the port |the neighbour's spec
|Held until accepted |`a_valid` and not `a_ready` -> in the next cycle, `a_valid`, and every A field
and any sideband `$stable` |the port |cheriot A1, C3a
|At most N outstanding |`MaxOutstanding` = N, so TL09 holds the limit and the list shrinks (DM10);
or, keeping the full list, `a_valid` -> `num_outstanding_o` < N, or `d_fire_o` |the parameter; or
`num_outstanding_o`, `d_fire_o` |cheriot A2
|Top source bits kept free |`a_valid` -> `a_source[7:5]` = 0 |the port |cheriot A9
|Answers in order |`d_valid` and `num_outstanding_o` != 0 -> `d_source` = `oldest_src_o`
|`num_outstanding_o`, `oldest_src_o` |cheriot A7
|Answers taken at once |`d_valid` -> `d_ready` |the port |cheriot C3b
|Requests eventually accepted, answers eventually given and taken |none to write: set `Liveness` to
1 in the liveness runs (TL17-TL19, [TL] §5) |the parameter |[TL] §5
|===

* *At most N, two forms that differ in one case:* with N requests outstanding, TL09 lets a request
  be presented only in a cycle where an answer to one of the N is taken. The assumption form also
  lets it be presented when only the new request is answered, in its own cycle: that request never
  counts, so N is never exceeded either way. TL09 is the stricter form and follows DM12's reading:
  the host cannot stop the device taking the request without answering it at once, so presenting
  it at N is already the breach. Its basis must cover that case: for cheriot A2, "a third request
  is presented only in the cycle an answer is taken". The parameter is also the cheaper form: the
  list then holds N entries.
* *Liveness:* [TL]'s forward progress is the ABVIP's own TL17-TL19, behind `Liveness`. A project
  writes only a stronger rule on top, such as an answer within N cycles, with its basis. Such a
  rule,
  like TL17-TL19, uses `s_eventually` or a bound: put an `s_eventually` in an
  `` `ifndef VERILATOR`` block inside `` `ifdef FPV_ON`` (sv-style.md, Lint), and turn it on only in
  liveness runs.
* *The DUT's side:* the ABVIP never checks the project's restrictions on what the DUT drives. A
  project that needs one, for example "the DUT answers in order", writes the same property as its
  own `assert_`.

The bound rules module form with every restriction above: the module and its bind file, lint-clean with
Verilator 5.048 `-Wall` and slang 11.0, with and without `FPV_ON`, in both run modes (`Liveness` 0
and 1):

// sv-file: lint:fpv_env_rules_example.sv | Environment rules module, with the assumptions on top
// sv-end

// sv-file: lint:fpv_env_bind_example.sv | Its bind file
// sv-end

'''

[[example_checker1]]
=== Example: cheriot_mem_sys checker 1

*Example only.* The checker 1 uarch owns this configuration
(link:{cms}/tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch.adoc[cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch.adoc]).
This example shows the ABVIP the way checker 1 uses it, copied by script from its checker
`tpchk_checker.sv` in `hw/ip/cheriot_mem_sys/fpv/tag_path/`, which holds all six:

* four ABVIPs on the ports the testbench plays, with the rules on top: `PlayHost` or
  `PlayDevice` in FPV, `CheckBoth` in simulation, where the real neighbour drives the port;
* two `CheckBoth` ABVIPs on the two links between real blocks (checker 1's decision D21, adopted
  by the user).

[cols="2,4,2,3,4",options="header"]
|===
|Instance |Port or link |Role |Parameters |Checker 1's rules on top ([CMS-DA], [CMS-TB])

|`u_abvip_core` |`cored_tl_d`, with its tag sideband |`PlayHost` |`MaxOutstanding` 2: A2 |A1, A9;
liveness run B: P5
|`u_abvip_xbar` |`cored_tl_h`, to `xbar_main` |`PlayDevice` |`MaxOutstanding` 4 |A7, A14, A15;
liveness run B: A10
|`u_abvip_m1` |2:1 tag arbiter, input 1: the blackboxed engine's tag filter |`PlayHost` |`SrcW` 7
|C3a, C11; liveness: C3b
|`u_abvip_tags` |RMW filter, downstream: the blackboxed tag access checker |`PlayDevice`
|`MaxOutstanding` 4 |C10; liveness run B: C1
|`u_abvip_m0`, on a link |2:1 tag arbiter, input 0: the core's tag filter, real |`CheckBoth`
|`SrcW` 7 |none: `CheckBoth` takes none
|`u_abvip_rmw`, on a link |RMW filter, upstream, after the tag clear squash |`CheckBoth`
|defaults |none
|===

* *A2 as a parameter:* `MaxOutstanding` 2 on `u_abvip_core` is assumption A2, the core's limit of
  two requests in flight, with A2 as its basis (DM10): a list of 2 entries instead of 256.
* *`MaxOutstanding` 4 on a played device:* there TL09 is asserted on the design, so the value
  sizes the list and checks checker 1's reasoning that the tag filter keeps three or fewer requests
  in flight to `xbar_main`, and the RMW filter one to the tag access checker.
* *`SrcW` 7 at both arbiter inputs:* the arbiter adds one source bit, and [TLUL] lets the top bit
  get lost (source bits). Behind the arbiter the RMW filter must return all 8 bits, so
  `u_abvip_rmw` keeps the default.
* *Blackboxed ends:* `u_abvip_m1` and `u_abvip_tags` assume the TL-UL rules on the outputs of
  blackboxed blocks, so these assumptions are contracts (<<reuse>>): each needs a unit that asserts
  the same rules on that block's port. Checker 1's contracts C1, C3a, C10 and C11 cover its own
  rules on top; none names the ABVIP's TL-UL rules on these two ports. To raise with checker 1's
  owner.
* *Expected failures, Suspected:* checker 1 records a suspected RTL issue on these links (U10 in its
  uarch, Proposed changes to other docs). The tag clear squash turns an engine's `Put` into a `Get`,
  so the engine's `Put` gets `AccessAckData` back (TL11 on `u_abvip_m1`), and a gapped mask can
  reach the RMW filter on a `Get` (TL06 on `u_abvip_rmw`; since DM9 any partial mask does). Not
  yet run in Jasper.
* Assumption labels follow checker 1's convention, `assume_<An or Cn>_<Rule>`. The checker also
  holds A3-A6, which are not TL-UL rules; they are left out below.
* Integrity stays free on every port.
* The SV below is copied from checker 1's files by `tools/embed_sv.py`, which also flags any change
  in them (`tools/verify.sh`). Checker 1 lints and elaborates these files itself, with its own
  `tools/verify.sh`.

// sv-items: ot:hw/ip/cheriot_mem_sys/fpv/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv | Checker 1's ABVIPs on the ports the TB plays, in tpchk_checker.sv | lines:^  // A TL-UL ABVIP on each port the testbench plays~lint_on PINCONNECTEMPTY
// sv-end

// sv-items: ot:hw/ip/cheriot_mem_sys/fpv/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv | Checker 1's CheckBoth ABVIPs, in tpchk_checker.sv | lines:^  // TL-UL rules on the links between real blocks //~lint_on PINCONNECTEMPTY
// sv-end

'''

[[selfcheck]]
=== Self-check plan

*Rule:* the ABVIP is verified like a design. Three questions decide whether it can be trusted:

. Does each rule mean the same as an assumption and as an assertion, in every role block: no copy
  error, and no state that differs by role?
. Can each assertion fail at all, or is it a tautology?
. Do the assumptions together still allow long, varied, legal traces, or do they over-constrain?

[cols="1,4,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Run |Set-up |Expected result |Answers

|S1 |`tlul_abvip_selfcheck` in each configuration below. `u_host` assumes the host rules and asserts
the device rules; `u_device` does the reverse, on the same wires; `u_check` asserts every rule
again. |every `assert_` proven, including all of `u_check`{empty}'s; every cover of the three
instances and every witness cover hit |1, 3
|S2 |configurations A, E and F, each twice, with Jasper switches only: `u_host`{empty}'s `assume_`
off, then `u_device`{empty}'s |every `assert_` of the instance whose assumptions stay on fails
with a CEX, except TL20-TL27, which cannot fail in Jasper (DM11); in E, TL17 with
`u_host`{empty}'s off, TL18 and TL19 with `u_device`{empty}'s; in F, TL28 to TL30 with `u_device`{empty}'s: no assertion is a tautology, and no role's
assumptions make the DUT's checks unfalsifiable (DM20) |2
|S3 |lint of every configuration: Verilator 5.048 `-Wall` and slang 11.0 (`tools/verify.sh`)
|clean: done, its SV file |-
|S4 |configuration A: the lane rows of lanes under `u_host`{empty}'s assumptions, and [TLPC]'s
sizeMatchesMask written apart from the ABVIP's lanes |every legal row's cover hit; every illegal
row's assertion and `assert_Self_SizeMatchesMask` proven |the rules mean their spec rows
|===

[cols="1,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Configuration |Parameters, the same on all three instances |What it shows

|A, base |`SrcW` 2, so `MaxOutstanding` is 4 |every rule; `cover_Src_Full` reached in a short trace;
the defaults allow a withdrawn request and out-of-order answers (`cover_Req_Withdrawn`,
`cover_Rsp_OutOfOrder`)
|B, small list |`SrcW` 2, `MaxOutstanding` 2 |TL09 binds before TL08 does; every witness cover
still hit
|C, full width |`SrcW` 8, `MaxOutstanding` 4 |sources that use all 8 bits
|D, defaults |`SrcW` 8, `MaxOutstanding` 256 |the sizes projects use; reported undetermined, with
its
bound, if it does not converge (DM15)
|E, liveness |configuration A with `Liveness` 1 |TL17-TL19 agree across the roles, in a liveness
run
|F, device contract |`SrcW` 2, `DevSameCycleRsp` 0, `DevMaxOutstanding` 1, `DevRspBound` 1 |TL28 to
TL30 agree across the roles; the list fills to the device's limit of 1
|===

*Why the small sizes stand for every size (DM15):* every list entry has the same logic, built by
one generate loop; `CntW` and `IdxW` follow from the parameters; nothing depends on a particular
entry or count except the list's two ends, which A and B reach at 4 and 2 entries; and C covers
every source bit. So a rule that holds at 2 to 4 entries holds at 256. Configuration D runs the
defaults as well.

Witness covers of the harness, beyond each instance's own covers (<<covers>>):

[cols="3,5",options="header"]
|===
|Cover |Long legal trace it shows

|`cover_Self_EightRsp` |`RspGoal` (8) answers taken: `num_rsp_q`, the harness's only flop (4 bits, saturating at 8), counts them
|`cover_Self_BackToBack` |four requests accepted in four cycles in a row
|`cover_Self_Streaming` |a request and an answer in every cycle, four cycles in a row
|`cover_Self_FillDrain` |the list fills to `MaxOutstanding`, then drains to empty within
`DrainCycles` cycles, one answer per cycle
|===

Lane rows of S4, from lanes, presented under `u_host`{empty}'s assumptions (32-bit bus):

[cols="4,3,2,2,4",options="header"]
|===
|Label |Opcode |Offset, size |Mask |Expected

|`cover_Self_RowGetWord` |`Get` |0, 2 |`1111` |legal: cover hit
|`cover_Self_RowPartialByte` |`PutPartialData` |1, 0 |`0010` |legal: cover hit
|`cover_Self_RowPartialHalf` |`PutPartialData` |2, 1 |`1100` |legal: cover hit
|`cover_Self_RowPartialGap` |`PutPartialData` |0, 2 |`1001` |legal: cover hit
|`cover_Self_RowFullByte` |`PutFullData` |3, 0 |`1000` |legal: cover hit
|`assert_Self_RowGetPartMask` |`Get` |2, 1 |`0100` |illegal by TL06: proven
|`assert_Self_RowGetNoMask` |`Get` |0, 2 |`0000` |illegal by TL06: proven
|`assert_Self_RowBadOpcode` |`3'h2` |0, 2 |`1111` |illegal by TL01: proven
|`assert_Self_RowGetSize3` |`Get` |0, 3 |`1111` |illegal by TL03: proven
|`assert_Self_RowUnaligned` |`PutPartialData` |1, 1 |`0110` |illegal by TL04: proven

* `u_check` shows that `CheckBoth` raises no false failure on a legal link: each of its rule
  assertions is assumed by `u_host` or `u_device`, so all must prove. Which property each label
  instantiates is checked by the check map script (<<check_map>>), not by a proof.
* If S1 does not converge on its full proof, helper `assert_Self_HelperSameList`
  (<<state_inventory>>) is the first to try.

==== Strategy and ledger

*Rule:* the self-check is one proof unit; every obligation it serves is closed by a run, a script or
a review, or is a gap with its reason (verification-strategy.md, VS-29).

* *Proof unit:* `tlul_abvip_selfcheck`, with its three `tlul_abvip` instances. No blackbox, no cut
  point, no contract.
* *Abstraction:* parameter reduction. Configurations A to C use 2 to 4 list entries and `SrcW` 2 or
  8, not the default 256 entries: approved, with the argument above and run D at the defaults
  (DM15).

[cols="4,5,2",options="header"]
|===
|Obligation |Closed by |Status

|each role block instantiates the right property, with the right prefix |`tools/checkmap.py`: 70
labels |done
|the assumed and asserted forms agree, and the assumptions do not over-constrain |S1:
`u_check`{empty}'s assertions, every cover, the witness covers |planned
|no assertion is a tautology, and no assumed form makes the other end's assertions unfalsifiable
|S2, TL20-TL27 excepted (DM11, DM20) |planned
|each request rule encodes its spec sentence |not by S1 or S2: an encoding error is assumed and
asserted alike. S4 checks the request rules against the lane rows, which `tools/doc_tables.py`
recomputes from the spec's definitions, and against [TLPC]'s sizeMatchesMask; the answer and
source rules rest on review against [TL] and [TLPC] |planned (S4 in the SV)
|the result holds at every size |the argument above (DM15), and run D |planned
|===
